title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A pretty easygoing edition: the Broncos squeaked out another close win, Druski had a fun first night hosting SNL, and Charlotte gets a few more sunny fall days before a cold front arrives. Jamaica's Gleaner ran a nice series on teaching more people to swim, and there's promising early science on psoriasis and gut health. The big business chatter is about Nvidia's CEO admitting to an affair.

stories.headline: Broncos edge Panthers 26-21 thanks to a rare late challenge
stories.summary: Denver beat Carolina 26-21 in Charlotte on Sunday for its fifth straight win. The turning point came when officials ruled that coach Sean Payton had thrown his challenge flag before the next snap. The review turned a Panthers incompletion at the 1-yard line into a Broncos interception. A late strip-sack by Nik Bonitto sealed it.
key_facts: Bo Nix threw for 237 yards and 2 TDs; Jonah Coleman ran for 57 yards and a score
Denver has won 16 straight one-score games and is 7-2, alone atop the AFC West
Carolina falls to 3-5 after three straight losses and plays at New Orleans next
Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle and CB Riley Moss left the game with concussions
stories.why: The Broncos keep finding ways to win close games, and Panthers fans saw a challenge play even the players didn't know was possible.

stories.headline: Druski's SNL debut brings the musical laughs
stories.summary: Comedian Druski hosted Saturday Night Live for the first time on Nov. 7, with The Strokes as musical guest. Standouts included "Proposal," where he keeps belting "she said yes" after the proposal is turned down, and a parody about a "socially conscious" hip-hop crew. He also played opposite Jane Wickline's Elizabeth Holmes in a sketch spoofing a Nathan Fielder-style documentary.
key_facts: Episode aired Saturday, Nov. 7, during SNL's season 52
Musical guest was The Strokes
Drake, Travis Scott and Quavo congratulated him when he was announced as host
stories.why: It's an easy, feel-good watch, and it showed Druski has real singing chops.

stories.headline: A Jamaican school makes swimming part of class
stories.summary: Fewer than 40% of Jamaicans aged 15 and up can swim without help. The Queen's School in St Andrew is one of a handful of schools that require swimming lessons. Students learn water confidence, floating and strokes. Teacher Georgina Boland says it's a safety skill and also a way for Jamaicans to enjoy their own beaches and rivers.
key_facts: All first- to third-form students take a term of swimming
Under 40% of Jamaicans 15+ can swim unassisted (OECD 2022 report, 2019 data)
Jamaica has about 120 rivers and streams and 70 public bathing beaches
stories.why: It's a practical effort to give kids a lifelong safety skill, plus a lot more fun at the beach.

stories.headline: Western Jamaica's young swimmers aim high despite few pools
stories.summary: Swim clubs in western Jamaica are building competitive programs despite a shortage of coaches and facilities. SailFish Swim Academy in St James says most top coaching talent stays in Kingston, so it has recruited coaches from Cuba. Running its own pool is costly, but the club keeps training going.
key_facts: SailFish Swim Academy was founded in 2015 at Wespow Park, Tucker, St James
At least five Cuban coaches have been recruited over the years
It trains in a 25-metre pool that is treated three times a week
stories.why: It's a nice look at a community working around real obstacles to help kids compete.

stories.headline: Why more Jamaican schools don't have pools: the cost
stories.summary: Pools are expensive to build and run, so most schools can't afford one, says Major Desmon Brown of the Calabar Old Boys' Association. Calabar High had Jamaica's first high school pool in 1953, but it stopped working by 1995. The Queen's School says upkeep runs over $80,000 a month and is covered through auxiliary fees.
key_facts: Building a pool can cost $5 million or more
Calabar's pool has been out of use since around 1995; principal Sian Wilson has said she plans to address it
A first-form student at Queen's pays $35,000 in auxiliary fees
stories.why: It explains the practical hurdle behind getting more young Jamaicans swimming.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits affair; company opens investigation
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted Sunday to an affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, whom reports describe as a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia has launched an independent security investigation. President Trump stood by him, calling him "an honorable guy." His wife of over 40 years, Lori Huang, has not commented.
key_facts: Huang has led Nvidia, now valued at about $4.5 trillion, for roughly 30 years
Jensen and Lori Huang have been married since 1985 and met at Oregon State University
The couple has donated to STEM education, including $50 million to Oregon State
disputed: Confirmed: Huang admitted the affair, and Nvidia opened an independent investigation
Not established: that Alice Huang is a spy; reports call her a "suspected" spy
Unclear: what, if anything, the investigation will find
stories.why: Huang is one of the most influential people in AI, so questions about security at Nvidia matter well beyond gossip.

stories.headline: Businessman Christopher Issa: 'There's no gold medal for doing the limbo'
stories.summary: Speaking at Webster Memorial United Church's 85th anniversary awards, S Hotels Jamaica CEO Christopher Issa said Jamaica has grown too comfortable with underperformance. He urged leaders and citizens to raise the bar, like in the high jump, on roads, hospitals and schools. His hope is that young people won't need to leave Jamaica to chase their dreams.
key_facts: Spoke Saturday at Webster Memorial United Church in St Andrew
Noted Jamaica marks 64 years of Independence this year
Called for priority on education, infrastructure, productivity, technology and healthcare
stories.why: It's a memorable call for higher standards that's sparking conversation about Jamaica's future.

stories.headline: Charlotte gets sunny fall days, then a cooldown
stories.summary: The western Carolinas can expect classic fall weather, with sunshine and mild temperatures through Wednesday. A cold front arrives after that and brings cooler conditions.
key_facts: Sunny and mild through Wednesday
Cold front brings cooler weather later in the week
stories.why: Good excuse to get outside early in the week, and maybe dig out a jacket for later.
